title: Negotiating and persuading / Nke a na-emepụta na nkwado
bridge: Na Spanish, anyị na-eme ka ndị mmadụ mee ihe ha n'okpuru ndoro doro na usoro doro na 'deberías' ma ọ bụ 'tienes que', na subjunctive na clauses na 'para que'. Na English, B2 na-enye ndoro doro na ọtụtụ na ndoro, na-eme ka ndoro doro na 'would', 'could', 'might' na 'I was wondering if...'. Ndoro ịgụ ụzọ doro na 'hacer una contraoferta' doro na 'to make a counteroffer' (enyi), mana verb 'to suggest' anaghị enwe subjunctive na English, ma ọ bụ na-akwado infinitive (suggest + infinitive). Nke a na-enye ndoro doro na 'tag questions' na ndoro na-agụ ụzọ na-agụ ụzọ na '¿no?', n'ihi na na English, ndoro na-akwado na auxiliary verb nke clause doro.
rule: Iji na-eme ka ndoro doro na English B2, ndoro na-eme ka: 1) Modals verbs na-arụ ụzọ na-arụ ụzọ: 'would' (I would appreciate...), 'could' (Could we...), 'might' (That might work). 2) Structures na-arụ ụzọ na-arụ ụzọ: 'I was wondering if...', 'Would it be possible to...?', 'If you could..., that would be...'. 3) Mmekọrịta na-arụ ụzọ na-arụ ụzọ: 'That's a fair point, but...', 'I see what you mean, however...'. 4) Mmekọrịta na-arụ ụzọ na-arụ ụzọ: 'What if we...?', 'How about...' + -ing, 'Would you be open to...?'. 5) Conditional na-arụ ụzọ na-arụ ụzọ: 'If we lowered the price, would you buy two?' (ndoro two conditional). Na-arụ ụzọ na-arụ ụzọ, ndoro na-eme ka phrases na 'Think of it this way...', 'The way I see it...', 'It's worth considering that...'. Nke a na-enye ndoro: na English, 'suggest' na 'recommend' na-akwado na that + subject + verb na form base (n'ihi na 's'), ma ọ bụ na gerund: 'I suggest that we wait' / 'I suggest waiting'. Subjunctive anaghị enwe na English nke doro na Spanish.

concept_examples.text: Could we possibly meet halfway on the price?
concept_examples.translation: Anyị nwere ike ịbanye n'ime ụzọ na ndoro?
concept_examples.phonetic: /kʊd wi ˈpɒsəbli miːt ˌhæfˈweɪ ɒn ðə praɪs/

concept_examples.text: I was wondering if you might consider a discount for bulk orders.
concept_examples.translation: Emeela m ka m na-akwado ike ịbanye n'ime ndoro na ndoro.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ wɒz ˈwʌndərɪŋ ɪf ju maɪt kənˈsɪdər ə dɪskaʊnt fɔː bʌlk ˈɔːrdərz/

concept_examples.text: What if we extend the deadline by a week? That could work for both of us.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na anyị na-enye ndoro ụbọchị anọ, ọ dịrị m ka ọ ga-eme ka ndoro doro.
concept_examples.phonetic: /wɒt ɪf wi ɪkˈstend ðə dedlaɪn baɪ ə wiːk ðæt kʊd wɜːrk fɔːr boʊθ əv ʌs/

concept_examples.text: If you agree to a lower price, we'll sign the contract today.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na ị na-agbakwunye ndoro, anyị na-enye contract ugbu a.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪf ju əˈɡriː tʊ ə loʊər praɪs wiːl saɪn ðə ˈkɒntrækt təˈdeɪ/

common_error.wrong: I suggest that we should wait until next week.
common_error.correct: I suggest that we wait until next week.
common_error.correct_alt: I suggest waiting until next week.
common_error.explanation: Ndoro na-eme ka ndoro na-eme ka 'sugiero que debamos esperar' na verb 'should'. Na English, n'okpuru 'suggest' (na 'recommend', 'propose'), ndoro na-akwado subjunctive na English, nke na-akwado na form base nke verb (n'ihi na 's' ma ọ bụ 'should'). Ndoro na-eme ka na gerund na-arụ ụzọ doro na alternative. Nke a na-enye ndoro na subjunctive na Spanish anaghị enwe n'okpuru na English, na English na-akwado na form base na-arụ ụzọ na-arụ ụzọ, ma ọ bụ na 'he/she/it'.

examples.original: Would it be possible to get an extension?
examples.phonetic: /wʊd ɪt bi ˈpɒsəbl tə ɡet ən ɪkˈstenʃən/
examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na ị nwere ike ịbanye n'ime ndoro ụbọchị anọ?

examples.original: I was wondering if you could lower the price.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ wɒz ˈwʌndərɪŋ ɪf ju kʊd ˈloʊər ðə praɪs/
examples.translation: Emeela m ka m na-akwado ike ịbanye n'ime ndoro.
examples.note: Nke a na-akwado 'I was wondering if...' na-adịghị mma na ndoro. M na-akwado 'I wondered' nke na-enye ndoro doro.

examples.original: Could we possibly agree on a different payment schedule?
examples.phonetic: /kʊd wi ˈpɒsəbli əˈɡriː ɒn ə ˈdɪfrənt ˈpeɪmənt ˈʃedjuːl/
examples.translation: Anyị nwere ike ịbanye n'ime ndoro ụbọchị anọ?
examples.note: 'Possibly' na-enye ndoro doro. Na Spanish, anyị na-eme '¿Podríamos quizás?', mana 'possibly' na-akwado n'okpuru subject.

examples.original: That's a fair point, but we can't go below ten percent.
examples.phonetic: /ðæts ə feər pɔɪnt bʌt wi kænt ɡəʊ bɪˈloʊ ten pəˈsent/
examples.translation: Nke a na-enye ndoro doro, mana anyị anaghị enwe ike ịbanye n'ime percent iri.
examples.note: Nkwenye ndoro nke ọ bụla ('That's a fair point') na-arụ ụzọ na-arụ ụzọ n'ihi na ị na-eme ka ndoro.

examples.original: If you agree to a longer contract, we could offer a better rate.

examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na ị na-agbakwunye contract ugbu a, anyị nwere ike ịbanye n'ime ndoro doro.
examples.note: Ndoro two conditional (if + past, would/could) na-arụ ụzọ na-arụ ụzọ na-arụ ụzọ na-arụ ụzọ.

examples.original: How about reducing the quantity instead of the price?
examples.phonetic: /haʊ əˈbaʊt rɪˈdjuːsɪŋ ðə ˈkwɒntəti ɪnˈsted əv ðə praɪs/
examples.translation: Kedu ka anyị na-enye ndoro na ndoro?
examples.note: 'How about + -ing' na-adịghị mma na ndoro na-arụ ụzọ na-arụ ụzọ.

examples.original: Think of it this way: a lower upfront cost saves you money in the long run.
examples.phonetic: /θɪŋk əv ɪt ðɪs weɪ ə loʊər ʌpˈfrʌnt kɒst seɪvz ju ˈmʌni ɪn ðə lɒŋ rʌn/
examples.translation: Jụọ ya n'ụzọ a: ndoro nke ntinye na-arụ ụzọ na-arụ ụzọ na-arụ ụzọ na-arụ ụzọ.
examples.note: Mmekọrịta 'Think of it this way' na-adịghị mma na ndoro na-arụ ụzọ na-arụ ụzọ.

examples.original: Would you be open to a trial period for three months?
examples.phonetic: /wʊd ju bi ˈoʊpən tʊ ə ˈtraɪəl ˈpɪəriəd fɔː θriː mʌnθs/
examples.translation: Anyị nwere ike ịbanye n'ime ndoro ugbu a ugbu a ugbu a?
examples.note: 'Open to' na-adịghị mma na ndoro na-arụ ụzọ na-arụ ụzọ, mana na-enye ndoro na 'dispuesto a considerar'.

examples.original: If we meet your deadline, will you extend the payment terms?
examples.phonetic: /ɪf wi miːt jɔːr dedlaɪn wɪl ju ɪkˈstend ðə ˈpeɪmənt tɜːmz/
examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na anyị na-enye ndoro ugbu a, anyị nwere ike ịbanye n'ime ndoro ugbu a ugbu a?
examples.note: Ndoro one conditional (if + present, will) na-arụ ụzọ na-arụ ụzọ na-arụ ụzọ na-arụ ụzọ na-arụ ụzọ.

examples.original: I'm confident we can find a solution that works for both sides.
examples.phonetic: /aɪm ˈkɒnfɪdənt wi kæn faɪnd ə səˈluːʃən ðæt wɜːks fɔːr boʊθ saɪdz/
examples.translation: A na-enye m ndoro na anyị nwere ike ịbanye n'ime ndoro ugbu a ugbu a ugbu a ugbu a.
examples.note: Anyị na-eme ka 'I'm confident' n'ihi na 'I think' na-enye ndoro na-arụ ụzọ na-arụ ụzọ na-arụ ụzọ.

title: Giving and justifying opinions in depth / Gịnị na-egosi na nkwụsị ike n'ime ndoro ndoro
bridge: Na Spanish, okpụrụ ụzọ dị mkpa bụ 'mụ nwere ike na' ma ọ bụ 'mụ na-eme' ma ọ bụ 'mụ na-akwado na' na-egosi na nkwụsị ike n'ime ndoro ndoro. Na English, iji egosi nkwụsị ike n'ime ndoro ndoro, ị ga-achọpụta okpuru ndoro ndoro dị ka 'the reason being', 'due to', 'given that', na nkọwa ndoro ndoro dị ka 'if... then...'. Gịnị adịghị mma bụ na-egosi nkwụsị ike n'ime ndoro ndoro na-akpọrọ 'según mi opinión' (na-emepụta 'according to my opinion' - enweghị ike, ọ bụrụ na ị na-akpọrọ 'in my opinion'). Na ndoro ndoro nke Spanish, na English, ụzọ ụzọ ndoro ndoro (would, could) dị mkpa maka ịmepụta nkwụsị ike na ịmepụta nkwanyere onwe ha n'ime ndoro ndoro.
rule: Iji egosi nkwụsị ike n'ime ndoro ndoro na English, ị ga-achọpụta: 1) Okpuru ndoro ndoro: 'In my view', 'From my perspective', 'I would argue that', 'It seems to me that'. 2) Nkwanyere onwe: 'The reason for this is', 'This is due to', 'Given that', 'Considering that'. 3) Nkwanyere ndoro: 'However', 'On the other hand', 'While it is true that...', 'Nevertheless'. 4) Nkọwa ndoro ndoro maka ịnweta: 'If... then', 'Unless...', 'Provided that...'. 5) Nkọwa ndoro ndoro nke cause-effect: 'This leads to', 'As a result', 'Consequently'. Ntuziaka B2: ị ga-ahụ maka ndoro ndoro ndoro na ndoro ndoro na-akpọrọ na ndoro ndoro na-akpọrọ na ndoro ndoro. Chọpụta ike na ịnweta nke adịbeghị n'ime ndoro ndoro na ịnweta nke adịbeghị n'ime ndoro ndoro (present perfect vs. past simple) mgbe ị na-egosi ndoro ndoro.

concept_examples.text: In my view, remote work has increased productivity, the reason being that employees avoid long commutes.
concept_examples.translation: N'ime m, ụlọ ọrụ ndoro ndoro nwere ike inyere ndoro ndoro n'ime ndoro ndoro, n'ihi na ndị mmadụ na-emeghị ihe ndoro ndoro n'ime ndoro ndoro.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪn maɪ vjuː, rɪˈmoʊt wɜːrk hæz ˈɪnkriːst ˌprɒdʌkˈtɪvəti, ðə ˈriːzn ˈbiːɪŋ ðæt ˌemploʊˈiːz əˈvɔɪd lɔːŋ kəˈmjuːts/

concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ wʊd ˈɑːrgjuː ðæt ɪnˈvestɪŋ ɪn ˌedʒuˈkeɪʃn jiːldz lɔːŋ tɜːrm ˈbenɪfɪts, ˈɡɪvn ðæt ɪt ɪmˈpruːvz ˈsoʊʃl moʊˈbɪləti/

concept_examples.translation: N'ime m, ụlọ ọrụ ndoro ndoro nwere ike inyere ndoro ndoro n'ime ndoro ndoro, n'ihi na ọ na-enyere ndoro ndoro n'ime ndoro ndoro n'ime ndoro ndoro.
concept_examples.phonetic: /frɒm maɪ pərˈspektɪv, ðə nuː ˈpɒləsi ɪz flɔːd, djuː tuː ðə fækt ðæt ɪt ɪɡˈnɔːrz ˈriːdʒənl ˈdɪfrənsɪz/

concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪt siːmz tuː miː ðæt wiː ʃʊd praɪˈɒrɪtaɪz rɪˈnjuːəbl ˈenərdʒi, ˈʌðəwaɪz wiː wɪl feɪs sɪˈvɪər ˈklaɪmət ˈkɒnsɪkwənsɪz/

common_error.wrong: According to my opinion, the government should do more for education.
common_error.correct: In my opinion, the government should do more for education.
common_error.correct_alt: From my point of view, the government should do more for education.
common_error.explanation: Na Spanish, anyị na-akpọrọ 'según mi opinión' (na-emepụta 'according to my opinion'), mana na English, a na-akpọrọ 'according to' na-akpọrọ na ndoro ndoro ndoro (according to the report). Okpuru ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro.

examples.original: In my view, the film was overrated.
examples.phonetic: /ɪn maɪ vjuː, ðə fɪlm wɒz ˌoʊvərˈreɪtɪd/

examples.note: Ị ga-achọpụta 'in my view' maka nkwanyere ndoro ndoro ndoro. Ị nwere ike ị ga-achọpụta 'to my mind' (n'ime m) mana ọ bụrụ na ọ bụrụ na ọ bụrụ na ọ bụrụ na ọ bụrụ.

examples.note: Ị ga-achọpụta 'due to' n'ime ndoro ndoro mana ọ bụrụ na ọ bụrụ na ọ bụrụ na ọ bụrụ na ọ bụrụ.

examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na ndoro ndoro nwere ike inyere ndoro ndoro n'ime ndoro ndoro, mana ọ bụrụ na ọ bụrụ na ọ bụrụ na ọ bụrụ.

translations.ig: Gịnị na-egosi na nkwụsị ike n'ime ndoro ndoro

title: Hypothesising about the past / Especular n'ụzọ ụfọdụ
bridge: Na Igbo, mgbakọ n'ụzọ ụfọdụ na-emepụta na 'nwere' ma ọ bụ 'nwere ike' na 'nwere ike', mana na English, ụdị mkpụrụ okwu ndoro ndoro bụ 'would have + past participle' na 'had + past participle' na third conditional. Ọtụtụ mmadụ na-eme ka mmadụ na-akpọ 'if would have' n'ime ụdị mkpụrụ okwu ahụ, mana na English, ụdị mkpụrụ okwu ahụ adịghị enweghi 'would'. N'ime English, ụdị mkpụrụ okwu ndoro ndoro bụ 'might have' ma ọ bụ 'could have' na-eme ka o si na mmadụ nwere ike ma ọ bụ ike ịnwere.
rule: Iji emepụta n'ụzọ ụfọdụ na English, ọ dịghị mkpụrụ okwu ndoro ndoro bụ 'third conditional' na ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro. Nke mbụ bụ: 'If + past perfect (had + participle), would have + past participle'. N'ịkpụ ụzọ: 'If I had studied, I would have passed'. Ọzọ dị, ụdị mkpụrụ okwu ndoro ndoro bụ 'could have' (ike ma ọ bụ ike), 'might have' (ike), 'should have' (ịdị n'ọnọdụ ma ọ bụ ịdị n'ọnọdụ). Na mgbakọ ndoro ndoro ma ọ bụ na usoro ndoro ndoro, ọ dịghị mkpụrụ okwu 'would have' n'ime ụdị mkpụrụ okwu 'if'. Na ndoro ndoro, ọ dịghị mkpụrụ okwu 'would' n'ime ụdị mkpụrụ okwu ahụ.

concept_examples.phonetic: /wiː kʊd hæv wʌn ðə mætʃ/

title: Expressing complex emotions / Nyeputa ndoro ndoro n'ime ndoro
bridge: N'igbo, anyị na-eme ka ndoro dị ka 'bụ' + okpukpere ma ọ bụ 'nwetara' ihe ndoro, mana n'Bekee, a na-eme ka ndoro dị ka okpukpere ndoro, okwu ndoro n'ime nkume na usoro ndoro. N'ihi na ndoro ndoro, ndoro ndoro na-eme ka ndoro dị ka 'I have fear of' n'ime okwu 'I'm afraid of'. N'ihi na Bekee na-eme ka ndoro ndoro dị ka 'frustrated' (ndoro) ma ọ bụ 'annoyed' (nwetara), ma ọ bụ 'overwhelmed' (ndoro ndoro) nke adịghị n'okpuru okpukpere nke na-eme ka ndoro ndoro. Tinye n'okpuru nkume na okpukpere ndoro nke na-eme ka ndoro ndoro na-eji n'ime okwu ndoro.
rule: Iji nyeputa ndoro ndoro n'Bekee, a na-eme ka ndoro ndoro dị ka: 1) Okpukpere ndoro n'ime nkume ndoro: 'angry about/at', 'frustrated with', 'disappointed in/with', 'excited about', 'worried about', 'ashamed of', 'proud of'. 2) Usoro n'ime 'feel' + okpukpere ma ọ bụ 'feel like' + okwu ndoro ndoro n'ime ndoro ndoro. 3) Okwu n'ime 'get' + okpukpere ndoro n'ime ndoro ndoro (get frustrated, get overwhelmed). 4) Okpukpere ndoro ndoro n'ime nkume ndoro n'ime ndoro ndoro: 'homesick', 'heartbroken', 'overwhelmed'. 5) Usoro ndoro ndoro n'ime okwu ndoro ndoro: 'on cloud nine' (ndoro ndoro), 'down in the dumps' (ndoro). Tinye na 'nervous' na-eme ka ndoro ndoro n'ime ndoro, 'anxious' nwere ike ịmalite n'ime ndoro ndoro ndoro; 'upset' dị mkpa karịa 'sad'. Mma ị na-eme ka 'I have' n'ime ndoro, n'ihi na n'ime okwu n'ime 'I have a feeling'.

title: Formal Writing: Reports and Emails / Nkwụsịrị ndoro: Akwụkwọ na email
bridge: Na Igbo, nkwụsịrị ndoro na-akwụ ịnwe nsogbu na-arụ ọrụ ndoro dị ike. Na English, nkwụsịrị ndoro na-akwụ ịnwe nkwado na nchekwa. Ọ bụrụ na ọ dịghị mma ịgbanwe naanị 'Le adjunto' ka 'I attach' (ọnwụghị) ma ọ bụrụ na ọ dịghị mma ịgbanwe ka 'Please find attached' ma ọ bụ 'I have attached'. N'okpuru, na English ndoro, ndoro ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro dị ike na-arụ ọrụ ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro. Na Igbo, ndoro ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro. Na English, ndoro ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro.
rule: Iji kwụsịrị ndoro ndoro na email na English na B2, ọ dị mma ịmepụta ndoro ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro. 1) Nkwado na nchekwa: 'Dear Mr. Smith', 'Dear Madam', 'Yours sincerely', 'Yours faithfully'. 2) Ndoro ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro: 'state' (na-eme ka 'say'), 'require' (na-eme ka 'need'), 'I would like to' (na-eme ka 'I want'), 'I am writing to inform you'. 3) Nkọwa ndoro: ndoro mbụ, ndoro nke na-egosi ndoro ndoro, na nkwuo ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro. 4) Ikwere ndoro ndoro: 'do not' na-eme ka 'don't', 'I would' na-eme ka 'I'd'. 5) Na akwụkwọ: jiri aha ndoro dị ike dịka 'Introduction', 'Findings', 'Recommendations', na ndoro ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro. 6) Ndoro ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro: 'Could you please...', 'I would appreciate...', 'Would it be possible to...?'. Chọpụta na na English ndoro, ndoro ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro.

common_error.correct_alt: I am writing to express my dissatisfaction with the service.
common_error.explanation: Ọ bụrụ na ị na-eme ka 'complaint' (nkwụwa) na-eme ka 'complain' (nkwụwa) na-eme ka 'to'. Na Igbo, 'ịkpọ' na-eme ka nkwụwa, mana na English, ọ dị mma ịme ka 'complain'. Ọzọ, ị na-eme ka 'me quejo de' na-eme ka 'I complain of' na-eme ka 'I complain about'. Iji chebe, chọpụta na na 'to' ọ dị mma ịme ka infinitive na-arụ ọrụ: 'to complain'.

examples.original: Dear Sir or Madam,
examples.phonetic: dɪə sɜːr ɔːr ˈmædəm,
examples.translation: Dear Sir or Madam,
examples.note: Ọ dị mma ịme ka na ị na-eme ka na ị na-eme ka na ị na-eme ka na ị na-eme ka.

examples.original: Dear Ms. García,
examples.phonetic: dɪə mɪz ɡɑːrˈsiːə,
examples.translation: Dear Ms. García,
examples.note: Na English, 'Ms.' na-eme ka ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro. Ikwere 'Mrs.' ma ọ bụrụ na ị na-eme ka na ị na-eme ka na ị na-eme ka.

examples.original: Yours faithfully,
examples.phonetic: jɔːz ˈfeɪθfʊli,
examples.translation: Yours faithfully (mgbe ị na-eme ka na ị na-eme ka na ị na-eme ka)
examples.note: Ọ dị mma ịme ka na ị na-eme ka na ị na-eme ka na ị na-eme ka na ị na-eme ka na ị na-eme ka.

examples.original: Yours sincerely,
examples.phonetic: jɔːz sɪnˈsɪəli,
examples.translation: Yours sincerely (mgbe ị na-eme ka na ị na-eme ka na ị na-eme ka)
examples.note: Ọ dị mma ịme ka na ị na-eme ka na ị na-eme ka na ị na-eme ka na ị na-eme ka.

examples.original: Could you please send me the updated schedule?
examples.phonetic: kʊd juː pliːz send miː ðiː ʌpˈdeɪtɪd ˈʃedjuːl?
examples.translation: Could you please send me the updated schedule?
examples.note: Na English ndoro, 'Could you please' na-eme ka ndoro ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro. Na Igbo, 'Podría' na-eme ka ndoro ndoro.

examples.original: I would appreciate your response at your earliest convenience.
examples.phonetic: aɪ wʊd əˈpriːʃieɪt jɔː rɪˈspɒns æt jɔː ˈɜːlɪəst kənˈviːniəns.
examples.translation: I would appreciate your response at your earliest convenience.
examples.note: A na-akpọ ndoro ndoro ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro. Na Igbo, ndoro ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro.

examples.original: Would it be possible to schedule a meeting next week?
examples.phonetic: wʊd ɪt biː ˈpɒsəbəl tə ˈʃedjuːl ə ˈmiːtɪŋ nekst wiːk?
examples.translation: Would it be possible to schedule a meeting next week?
examples.note: A na-akpọ ndoro ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro. Na Igbo, 'sería posible' na-eme ka ndoro ndoro, mana na English, ndoro ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro.

examples.original: The purpose of this report is to analyze the sales data for the third quarter.
examples.phonetic: ðə ˈpɜːpəs əv ðɪs rɪˈpɔːt ɪz tə ˈænəlaɪz ðə seɪlz ˈdeɪtə fɔː ðə θɜːd ˈkwɔːtə.
examples.translation: The purpose of this report is to analyze the third-quarter sales data.
examples.note: Na English ndoro, 'the purpose of this report is to...' na-eme ka ndoro ndoro ndoro. Na Igbo, 'El propósito de este informe es...' mana ndoro ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro.

examples.original: It was found that customer satisfaction has increased by 15%.
examples.phonetic: ɪt wɒz faʊnd ðæt ˈkʌstəmər ˌsætɪsˈfækʃən hæz ɪnˈkriːst baɪ fɪfˈtiːn pəˈsent.
examples.translation: It was found that customer satisfaction has increased by 15%.
examples.note: Na English ndoro, ndoro ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro. Na Igbo, 'se encontró que' na-eme ka ndoro ndoro.

examples.original: Based on the findings, we recommend implementing a new training program.
examples.phonetic: beɪst ɒn ðə ˈfaɪndɪŋz, wiː ˌrekəˈmend ˈɪmplɪməntɪŋ ə njuː ˈtreɪnɪŋ ˈprəʊɡræm.
examples.translation: Based on the findings, we recommend implementing a new training program.
examples.note: Na English, 'recommend + gerund' (recommend implementing) na-eme ka ndoro ndoro. Na Igbo, 'recomendamos implementar' na-eme ka ndoro ndoro. Chọpụta na ị na-eme ka 'recommend to implement' na English ndoro; mana 'recommend implementing' na-eme ka ndoro ndoro.

examples.original: In conclusion, the project was delivered on time and within budget.
examples.phonetic: ɪn kənˈkluːʒən, ðə ˈprɒdʒekt wɒz dɪˈlɪvəd ɒn taɪm ənd wɪðɪn ˈbʌdʒɪt.
examples.translation: In conclusion, the project was delivered on time and within budget.
examples.note: A na-akpọ 'in conclusion' na-eme ka ndoro ndoro. Na Igbo, 'en conclusión' na-eme ka ndoro ndoro, mana ndoro ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro na-arụ ọrụ ndoro.
